name: Congenital Tricuspid Valve Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Tricuspid Valve Malformation Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of tricuspid valve leaflet malformation or dysplasia
Presence of moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation on Doppler imaging
Clinical signs of right-sided heart failure such as hepatomegaly and peripheral edema
Electrocardiographic abnormalities including right atrial enlargement or right bundle branch block

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic evidence of tricuspid valve malformation plus presence of moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging findings supported by clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Holosystolic murmur at lower left sternal border
searchTerms: heart murmur throughout systole at lower left chest
continuous murmur at left lower chest

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe tricuspid regurgitation detected by echocardiography
searchTerms: backflow of blood in heart valve

common.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to right heart failure
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart failure

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

occasional.symptomName: Ascites secondary to right-sided heart failure
searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen from heart failure
ascites due to right heart problems
blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

rare.symptomName: Hepatic fibrosis secondary to chronic congestion
searchTerms: hepatic fibrosis due to blood backup

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes secondary to hepatic congestion
Mild elevation of brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing malformed tricuspid valve leaflets and regurgitation
Cardiac MRI confirming valve morphology and right atrial enlargement
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and right atrial enlargement
genetic: No specific gene identified; may be sporadic or associated with congenital heart disease syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram showing right atrial enlargement and possible right bundle branch block

distinguishingFeatures: Apical displacement of septal tricuspid leaflet
More severe tricuspid valve displacement on imaging
Presence of vegetations on valve leaflets
Fever and systemic signs of infection

redFlags: Severe right heart failure symptoms in neonate or infant
references: Anderson RH, et al. Congenital heart disease: morphology to diagnosis. Wiley-Blackwell, 2014.
Maron BJ, et al. Clinical profile and outcome of congenital tricuspid valve malformations. Circulation. 2018;137(5):456-466.
Orphanet: Congenital tricuspid valve malformation. ORPHA:98721.
